facts.text: The guide labels this as the second of three typical short-form mass timber examples.

The described project is new residential construction, 7 storeys, Group C major occupancy, with proposed mass timber construction; the building complex area is stated to exceed the 1500 m2 limit for a single 6-storey combustible building.

The example cites Sentence 3.1.10.2.(2) of the BC Building Code 2012 and objectives F03-OS1.2, F03-OP1.2 and F03-OP3.1. It proposes a cross-laminated timber firewall where the stated acceptable solution uses noncombustible materials.

The guide says the rationale relied primarily on relevant fire tests for the required fire-resistance rating and discusses structural independence, penetrations, openings, connections and differential shrinkage.
